research_notes: Seek court and Taylor and Scott appointment/hours/leave evidence, Denman practice workload and cessation records, and identity/dates of brief corporate-law role; resolve March–June 1998 transition and overlaps with council, party and community governance.

2026-09-29 initial avenues: NSW detailed biography, inaugural speech indexed passages, BenchTV professional profile, NSW Bar Association interview, contemporary retrospective press and explicit full-time searches. APH direct opening failed; frozen roster contains no occupations. State record supplies missing month dates.

NSW Bar article calls Shoebridge's Legislative Council appointment 2008; official state service record establishes 7 September 2010. Preserve correct official date and do not propagate the article's apparent typo. Its first-person cessation account is separately useful.

Corporate-law interview is a lead with unnamed employer; do not infer exact dates from the March–June 1998 gap. Retained practising certificate and self-represented litigation are not evidence of continuing commercial employment. Month precision and unknown hours prevent headline calculation under the approved methodology.

2026-10-01 systematic follow-up: reopened NSW biography and recovered full inaugural speech using its replacement file link; reviewed NSW Bar interview, targeted corporate-firm and deputy-mayor searches, RAS employer description and contemporary ABC index. Added previously missing RAS work, court-duration discrepancy and deputy-mayor point evidence. Searches did not name the short corporate-law employer or establish workload/leave; do not repeat identical searches without new leads.

Next evidence priorities: RAS payroll/seasonal appointment records and exact entity; Family Court associate appointment/cessation records resolving speech versus biography; Taylor and Scott/Denman hours, breaks and departure records; corporate-firm name; council minutes for deputy-mayor boundaries. No dates inferred from career gaps; all headline totals remain null.

Second follow-up2October2026: targeted corporate-law employer/Denman and council-boundary searches yielded no new supported employment hours, breaks or employer name. Wikipedia List of mayors of Woollahra supplies primary leads: Council Meeting Minutes13September2004 and Extraordinary Council Meeting Minutes7September2005, archived8September2006. Web click calls to its council/archive references returned Internal Error: Unable to resolve click call due to invalid arguments; underlying minutes were not retrieved. Secondary claimed dates13September2004–7September2005 remain leads, not adopted as verified primary endpoints. Contact-data aggregator January boundaries discarded in favour of official March2003–September2010 legal-practice dates. Current leadership news concerns parliamentary politics and does not resolve pre-parliament employment; no frozen roster changes. Continue with archived original council minutes, corporate-law employer evidence and individual court/firm appointment and hours records.

Third follow-up3October2026: recovered the exact archived Woollahra council PDF locations for the13September2004 meeting (Sept13councilmins04.pdf, capture20060908173714) and7September2005 mayoral election meeting (sept7-05mayorelectmins.pdf, capture20060908233629). The archive shells confirm captures and meeting metadata, but the embedded first PDF timed out and indexed search did not expose either resolution text. The secondary office table still reports13September2004–7September2005, but without retrieved primary contents those dates remain leads and are not written into the spell. Repeated exact-name searches also found no court appointment instrument, Taylor and Scott/Denman hours or breaks, or name of the brief corporate-law employer. Advance the cursor; retry the two archived PDFs only if archive access changes or a council catalogue copy appears.

Fourth follow-up4October2026 found no indexed resolution text for the two archived Woollahra minute filenames and did not improve Taylor and Scott or Denman boundaries/hours. It did recover a previously omitted early job: a March2022 Sydney Morning Herald interview reports nursing-home night shifts during Shoebridge's latter high-school years. The original article URL returned a non-retryable open error, but its exact link and article text were publicly reproduced on Reddit. Employer, duties, dates, pay, hours, leave and control remain unknown; accompanying odd jobs were not classified as employment without payment evidence.

Follow-up2026-10-04: New first-person Sydney Criminal Lawyers interview exposes a six-year Taylor & Scott recollection against the official June1998–March2003 interval; retained as a material chronology discrepancy requiring personnel records. The same interview repeats the three-year Baker recollection and confirms no private practice as an MP. Displayed2020 update is not original interview timing. Nursing-home identity searches returned generic current recruitment, not Shoebridge employment; admissions and current chambers do not establish historical hours. No old archive-PDF retries without changed access; council minute contents remain unresolved. Next leads: original firm personnel/payroll chronology and court associate instruments.
